clips.text_zh: Bloomberg話七成美國人 paycheck to paycheck。最有錢嗰5%先至過得爽。底層50%得2.5%財富。我哋呢啲咪一樣，30歲單身返工儲錢睇唔到盡頭。prop firm又輸緊，真係好撚灰。
clips.text_en_b1: Bloomberg says the bottom 70% of Americans live paycheck to paycheck. Only the top 5% are doing well. The bottom 50% own 2.5% of the wealth. Many people with higher income are also struggling now. Everyone else has cut spending. The gap between rich and poor keeps getting wider.
clips.text_en_b2: Bloomberg has reported that roughly seventy percent of Americans are essentially living paycheck to paycheck, with only the top five percent genuinely thriving. Meanwhile, the bottom half of the population controls a mere 2.5 percent of total wealth, and the chasm separating the ultra-wealthy from ordinary workers continues to widen. The original poster, a single thirtysomething who is actively grinding away, openly admits that the grind feels endless, and with a prop firm account currently bleeding money, the frustration is palpable and completely understandable.
clips.text_en_c1: According to a Bloomberg report, roughly seventy percent of Americans now find themselves living paycheck to paycheck, a figure that has prompted considerable debate on /biz/. While the top five percent appear largely insulated from these pressures, the bottom half of the population controls a mere 2.5 percent of total wealth, a disparity that continues to widen. Anons argue that even households once considered middle-class have begun trimming discretionary expenditure, suggesting the squeeze is no longer confined to the genuinely impoverished. The poster, a single thirtysomething who is hemorrhaging capital on a proprietary trading firm, describes the situation as utterly bleak, with no realistic end in sight.
clips.text_en_c2: Bloomberg has reported that roughly seventy percent of Americans are now living paycheck to paycheck, a figure that lays bare the precariousness of the lower seven deciles. While the uppermost five percent continue to enjoy considerable comfort, the bottom half of the population commands a meagre 2.5 percent of aggregate wealth, a disparity that has only widened over recent years. Even those who once considered themselves comfortably middle-class find themselves trimming discretionary expenditure, deferring maintenance, and quietly bracing for the next bill. The wealth chasm, in short, has become a yawning abyss, one in which an entire generation of thirty-something professionals, single and gainfully employed, save assiduously yet glimpse no horizon. For those punting on prop firms, the calculus is even more unforgiving: capital erodes, conviction falters, and the end remains stubbornly out of sight.

clips.text_zh: 有錢但抑鬱 定 窮但開心？我揀有錢。依家咩都冇又唔開心，真係double loss。廢物一個，唯有all in prop firm望翻身。考牌都未搞掂，wtf。
clips.text_en_b1: Would you rather be rich and depressed or poor and happy? The thread argues most people in /biz/ are already poor and depressed, so the choice is fake. The real question is just how much more pain you can take before the account blows. Some anons say take the red pill and stop trading.
clips.text_en_b2: The thread poses a deliberately provocative question: would you rather be wealthy and miserable, or broke and content? Most anons, however, point out that the choice is essentially meaningless, because they are already broke and miserable, making any further losses feel like a double loss. While some are holding out for that one moonshot, others have grown thoroughly disillusioned and are urging the original poster to take the red pill and walk away from trading entirely before it completely destroys them.
clips.text_en_c1: The thread poses a deceptively simple dilemma: would you prefer to be affluent yet chronically miserable, or impoverished but content? Most respondents, already familiar with the latter condition, dismiss the question as largely hypothetical, pointing out that for the average /biz/ denizen it represents a double loss. Their genuine concern is not the philosophical trade-off but rather how much additional drawdown one can endure before the trading account is inevitably blown. A handful of voices, however, advocate for what they term the red pill: stepping away from the markets entirely and confronting the underlying issues instead.
clips.text_en_c2: The thread's central conceit—whether one would prefer affluence laced with melancholy or poverty tempered by joy—is, the anons contend, a spurious dichotomy. Most who frequent the board already inhabit the latter condition without the compensating consolation, rendering the hypothetical a matter of intellectual exercise rather than lived reality. The genuine question, one poster observes, is not which state to choose but rather how much additional torment one can endure before the account is inevitably liquidated. A handful of respondents counsel surrender: abandon the prop firm, cease trading, swallow the red pill. Yet the original poster, mired in study and stalling on examinations, presses on regardless, reasoning that without concentrated exposure there exists no plausible path to recovery, even if that path remains largely illusory.

clips.text_en_b2: Anthropic has once again insisted that Claude possesses something resembling a soul, while the Pope has publicly pushed back, apparently dedicating an entire book to systematically dismantling the claim. Unsurprisingly, the /g/ thread treats the whole debate as fairly absurd, with one anon quipping that if an LLM counts, then surely a sleep-deprived civil engineering student pulling all-nighters before the FE exam must count too. The consensus is that the real concern should be safety.
clips.text_en_c1: Anthropic's latest marketing push appears to imbue Claude with a quasi-mystical sense of self, a claim the Pope has formally refuted, reportedly devoting an entire book to the rebuttal. Unfazed, Anthropic continues to insist that something resembling a soul is emerging within these systems. The /g/ thread greets both parties with the usual contempt, with one anonymous poster remarking that if LLMs possess souls, then so too must the average 3am contributor. Beneath the irony lies a more substantive anxiety, namely that the prevailing discourse has wandered into theology when the urgent questions concern safety.
clips.text_en_c2: Anthropic's increasingly bold assertion that Claude possesses something resembling a soul has drawn an ecclesiastical counterpunch from the Vatican, whose latest publication devotes considerable ink to dismantling the premise. The exchange, which might otherwise read as theology pitched against marketing, has been gleefully lampooned across /g/, where posters find the entire spectacle faintly absurd. One anon, with characteristic economy, observed that neither large language models nor the average insomniac contributor to the board can plausibly claim a soul, least of all at three in the morning. Beneath the irreverence, however, lurks a more substantive anxiety: the question of safety, alignment, and the consequences of anthropomorphic projection. The theology, in other words, is a distraction; what actually matters is whether the engineers know what they have built.

The /pol/ thread treats it as a breakdown of current events, not a prediction. Anons link his X post and argue about whether Musk is serious or just posting for engagement. clips.text_en_b2: Elon Musk has taken to X once again, this time warning that Europe is heading into full-blown white genocide territory and that widespread slaughter is essentially inevitable at this point. Predictably, /pol/ has latched onto the comments and is running with them hard, treating it less as a prediction and more as a description of the current state of affairs. clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk has once again taken to X to declare that Europe is veering into what he termed white genocide territory, predicting that the continent will eventually witness widespread slaughter. The /pol/ thread, predictably, has descended into its customary incoherence, though sharper observers note that the post is best understood not as prophecy but as a commentary on present-day civilisational decay. clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk has once again taken to X to declare that Europe is sliding into what he termed 'white genocide territory,' a phrase he has used previously to describe demographic and civilisational anxieties. His latest post warns that the continent will, in due course, witness widespread slaughter unless present trajectories are reversed. The /pol/ thread treats the remark less as prophecy than as a diagnostic of the present moment, parsing his motives with the weary scepticism of an audience long familiar with his rhetorical flourishes. Some anons argue he is simply chumming the waters for engagement, while others maintain that his pronouncements, however theatrical, reliably move markets. The observer's interest, per the original poster, lies squarely in the downstream effect upon DOGE and Tesla valuations whenever Musk deigns to opine.

clips.text_zh: /fit/話Powershitting Big 3唔夠，新手就係中招。淨係deadlift bench squat，lift上咗但肥到睇唔到自己雞雞。我都係，肥仔信叫我加cardio，等我下個禮拜開始sled push先。
clips.text_en_b1: Powershitting and the Big 3 are not enough. The thread says newbies fall into this trap. Obese lifters who cannot see their own dick or jog half a mile will still tell you to lift heavy and eat big. The poster wasted years doing strength-only training and looked worse. Conditioning and cardio matter too.
clips.text_en_b2: According to the /fit/ thread, fixating exclusively on the Big 3 compounds and a powershitting routine is a classic rookie mistake that inevitably backfires. Newbies pile on the deadlifts, bench, and squats, convinced that eating big is the answer, only to end up obese and unable to even see their own equipment. The original poster wasted years on strength-only training and ended up looking considerably worse, with fellow anons now pushing sled work and proper cardio as a way out.
clips.text_en_c1: The /fit/ consensus holds that an exclusive focus on powershitting and the so-called Big Three represents a classic novice trap, one that the original poster fell into for several years. Endless deadlifts, bench presses, and squats drove his numbers upward while his body composition deteriorated to the point where he could no longer see his own genitals. The thread skewers the fat powerlifter archetype, individuals who cannot jog half a mile yet insist that newcomers should eat aggressively and pile on weight. Conditioning, the poster concludes, is non-negotiable, and he plans to begin sled pushes next week.
clips.text_en_c2: The /fit/ consensus is unambiguous: an exclusive devotion to powershitting and the so-called Big Three movements—deadlift, bench, and squat—constitutes a rite of passage that doubles as a trap for the earnest novice. Aficionados accumulate iron, hoist ever-heavier loads, and, in the process, attain a physique that, while undeniably strong, is frequently accompanied by an adipose profile so pronounced that the subject cannot glimpse his own anatomy, let alone jog a half-mile without distress. The original poster confesses to having squandered years upon this strength-only regimen and emerged looking markedly worse for it, a cautionary admission that has galvanised the thread. Conditioning, sled pushes, judicious cardio—these, the consensus holds, are no longer optional adjuncts but rather indispensable components of any coherent programme.

clips.text_zh: 點解nips鍾意 bully 情侶但又唔放埋入動漫？Nagatoro係少數。我本身睇Gundam 00同Demon Slayer多，呢類校園戇戇嘢唔太啱我。lol。
clips.text_en_b1: Why do Japanese creators like bully couples but never put them into actual anime or manga? Nagatoro is the only example the OP can think of. Anons reply with other titles like Ijiranaide, Nagatoro-san. Some say the trope is overused and they are bored of tsundere heroines in 2026 already.
clips.text_en_b2: The thread raises a genuinely interesting question: why do Japanese creators so clearly adore the bully romance dynamic, yet almost never commit to it in finished anime or manga adaptations? Nagatoro-san remains the standout example that everyone inevitably circles back to, though anons have helpfully thrown in Ijiranaide and a few other titles for good measure. Others, however, are thoroughly sick of the tsundere heroine trope and openly declare that they are completely burned out on it by 2026.
clips.text_en_c1: The original poster raises an intriguing cultural observation, namely why Japanese creators remain so enamoured with the bully romance dynamic yet so rarely commit it to fully realised anime adaptations. Nagatoro-san stands as a rare exception, a title the thread enthusiastically endorses alongside suggestions such as Ijiranaide.
